questions.question: The tribal festival of Bhagoria is traditionally celebrated a week prior to which Hindu festival?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Holika Dahan**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The tribal festival of **Bhagoria** is celebrated predominantly by the **Bhil** and **Bhilala tribes** of the Indian states of **Madhya Pradesh** and **Maharashtra**.
 
• It is traditionally celebrated a week prior to the Hindu festival of **Holika Dahan**, which marks the beginning of the **spring season**.
 
• **Bhagoria Haat:** The festival is celebrated in the form of a fair known as the **Bhagoria Haat**, which acts as a marketplace and marriage fair where eligible young individuals choose their life partners.
 
• The celebration involves vibrant cultural activities, including tribal dance, music, and rituals that reflect the rich **tradition and customs** of these communities.
 
• The name "Bhagoria" is derived from the word **'Bhag' (to run away)**, symbolizing the tradition where couples elope and later gain acceptance from their families.
 
• The festival coincides with agricultural activities, marking the **completion of harvesting** and symbolizing prosperity and joy.
 
• **Holika Dahan:** This festival, also known as **Chhoti Holi**, is celebrated one day before **Holi** to signify the victory of good over evil, particularly the mythological story of **Prahlada** and **Holika**.
 
• The association of Bhagoria with Holika Dahan highlights the tribal communities' integration of their customs with broader Hindu festivals. *Hence, the correct answer is Holika Dahan.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Bhagoria Festival:**

 
 
• The Bhagoria festival is an integral part of the **indigenous culture** of the Bhil and Bhilala tribes, celebrated with enthusiasm and joy.
 
• **Location:** It is primarily celebrated in the **Jhabua** and **Alirajpur districts** of Madhya Pradesh and in parts of Maharashtra.
 
• The festival serves as an occasion for **social bonding** and allows tribal communities to showcase their unique traditions.
 
 
 
• **Holika Dahan:**
 
 
• **Date:** Holika Dahan occurs on the **Purnima (full moon)** night of the Hindu lunar month of **Phalguna**, generally in **February or March**.
 
• It symbolises the **victory of good over evil**, commemorating the tale of **Prahlada**, a devotee of Lord Vishnu, and Holika, his evil aunt.
 
• The festival is celebrated by lighting bonfires and performing rituals to cleanse negativity and bring prosperity.
 
 
 
• **Tribal Festivals:**
 
 
• Tribal festivals like Bhagoria reflect the **distinct cultural heritage** of indigenous communities in India.
 
• They often coincide with agricultural cycles, emphasizing the importance of **nature and community** in tribal life.
 
• Other notable tribal festivals include **Hornbill Festival** in Nagaland and **Baneshwar Fair** in Rajasthan.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Distinctive Cultural Practices:**

 
 
• **Bhagoria Haat** is a rare festival that combines social, cultural, and economic aspects, serving as a **marriage fair** and a market for tribal communities.
 
• The vibrant costumes, traditional music, and colorful rituals during Bhagoria showcase the **rich tribal heritage** of the region.
 
 
 
• **Connection with Holika Dahan:**
 
 
• The timing of Bhagoria, a week before Holika Dahan, integrates tribal festivities with the broader Hindu tradition, reflecting cultural **syncretism**.
 
• Both festivals signify **joy, renewal, and the celebration of life**, highlighting the importance of community and tradition.

questions.question: Which Mughal mausoleum does not strictly follow the conventional square-based hasht-bihisht architectural layout?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Akbar’s Tomb at Sikandra**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Akbar’s Tomb at Sikandra** is one of the most remarkable mausoleums built during the Mughal period but stands out because it does not follow the **conventional square-based hasht-bihisht architectural layout**.
 
• **Hasht-bihisht** refers to the "eight-paradise" layout, a symmetrical design commonly used in Mughal architecture, characterized by eight chambers surrounding a central space.
 
• The **layout of Akbar’s Tomb** deviates from this norm as it uses a **tiered pyramid-like structure**, with each tier becoming progressively smaller as it ascends, topped by an open terrace rather than a dome. *Hence, it does not follow the standard hasht-bihisht layout.*
 
• The **tomb** is located in **Sikandra**, near Agra, and was designed by Akbar himself during his lifetime. However, his son, Jahangir, completed its construction in **1613**.
 
• Unlike other Mughal tombs, the use of **red sandstone and marble**, along with extensive ornamentation, gives Akbar's Tomb a unique identity.
 
• The **design of Akbar’s Tomb** reflects his philosophy of religious tolerance, with elements from both Hindu and Islamic architectural styles.
 
• The garden surrounding the tomb follows the **Charbagh layout**, a traditional Persian garden style commonly adopted in Mughal architecture. *Hence, the correct answer is Akbar’s Tomb at Sikandra.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Humayun’s Tomb:**

 
 
• It is located in **Delhi** and was commissioned by Humayun's wife, **Bega Begum**, in **1569–1570**.
 
• It is the first Mughal tomb to use the **hasht-bihisht layout** extensively, with a central dome and symmetrical design. This tomb later influenced the construction of the **Taj Mahal.**
 
 
 
• **Tomb of Itimad-ud-Daulah:**
 
 
• This tomb, located in **Agra**, was commissioned by Noor Jahan for her father, Mirza Ghiyas Beg, in **1622–1628**.
 
• It is often referred to as the "Baby Taj" and is renowned for its extensive use of **white marble** and intricate **inlay work**.
 
• The **hasht-bihisht layout** is followed here, with a central hall surrounded by smaller chambers.
 
 
 
• **Safdarjung’s Tomb:**
 
 
• It is located in **Delhi** and was built in **1754** for Safdarjung, a Nawab of Awadh.
 
• The tomb follows the **hasht-bihisht plan** and is noted for its symmetrical layout, central dome, and large Charbagh garden.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Key Features of Hasht-Bihisht:**

 
 
• The layout consists of a central chamber surrounded by **eight smaller chambers**, symbolizing the eight levels of paradise in Islamic cosmology.
 
• This symmetrical design is a hallmark of Mughal architecture and is seen in notable tombs like the **Taj Mahal** and **Humayun’s Tomb.**
 
 
 
• **Significance of Akbar’s Tomb:**
 
 
• The tomb reflects **Akbar's secular ideologies** and his efforts to integrate elements of different architectural styles.
 
• Its deviation from the traditional Mughal tomb design highlights Akbar's unique vision and his influence on Mughal architecture.

questions.question:
Read the following statements carefully:

Statement 1: Harappan seals were generally carved from locally sourced steatite.

Statement 2: These seals commonly depict animals along with undeciphered symbols.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Both Statement 1 and Statement 2.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Statement 1:** Harappan seals were generally carved from locally sourced steatite.

 
 
• The **Harappan Civilization**, also known as the Indus Valley Civilization, was known for its advanced urban planning and craftsmanship. One of its most remarkable artifacts is the seals.
 
• The seals were primarily made from **steatite**, a soft stone that could be easily carved and hardened by firing. This material was locally available in the region, making it an ideal choice for artisans. *Hence, this statement is correct.*
 
 
 
• **Statement 2:** These seals commonly depict animals along with undeciphered symbols.
 
 
• Harappan seals are characterized by their intricate carvings, which often include **depictions of animals** such as bulls, elephants, rhinoceroses, and tigers. These animals are thought to have held religious or cultural significance for the Harappan people.
 
• In addition to animals, the seals also feature **short inscriptions or symbols** that remain undeciphered to this day. These symbols are believed to represent a script or pictorial language used by the Harappans. *Hence, this statement is also correct.*
 
 
 
• ***Thus, both statements are correct.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Harappan Seals:**

 
 
• **Material:** Made from steatite, faience, terracotta, and sometimes copper, the seals were typically square or rectangular in shape.
 
• **Purpose:** The seals are thought to have been used for multiple purposes, including trade, identification, and possibly religious rituals.
 
• **Symbols:** The inscriptions on the seals might represent a script, but they remain undeciphered, making it challenging to fully understand their significance.
 
 
 
• **Animal Depictions:**
 
 
• Common animals depicted include the **unicorn** (a mythical creature often seen on Harappan seals), bull, elephant, rhinoceros, and buffalo.
 
• These animals may have had symbolic or religious significance, possibly representing various deities or cultural beliefs.
 
 
 
• **Uses of Seals:**
 
 
• Seals were likely used for **trade and administrative purposes**, such as marking goods for identification or ownership.
 
• They may have also served as amulets or symbols of status, given their intricate designs and artistic quality.
 
 
 
• **Important Examples:**
 
 
• One of the most famous seals is the **Pashupati Seal**, which depicts a figure seated in a yogic posture surrounded by animals, possibly representing a proto-Shiva figure.
 
• Another example is the unicorn seal, which is unique to the Harappan Civilization and indicates the advanced artistic skills of its people.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Key Features of Harappan Civilization:**

 
 
• **Time Period:** The Harappan Civilization flourished around 2500–1900 BCE.
 
• **Geographical Spread:** It covered modern-day Pakistan and parts of northwest India, with major sites like **Harappa, Mohenjo-Daro, Lothal, and Dholavira**.
 
• **Trade:** Harappans engaged in extensive trade with regions like Mesopotamia, using seals to mark and identify goods.
 
 
 
• **Challenges in Deciphering Harappan Script:**
 
 
• The script on the seals consists of short inscriptions, usually 4–5 symbols long, making it difficult to decode.
 
• The lack of a bilingual inscription, like the Rosetta Stone for Egyptian hieroglyphs, has further complicated efforts to understand the Harappan script.

questions.question: The medieval coin known as “Dehliwal” was issued under the rule of which dynasty?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Tomaras**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The medieval coin known as **“Dehliwal”** was issued under the rule of the **Tomara dynasty**, which established its reign in Delhi during the early medieval period.
 
• The **Tomaras** were one of the earliest rulers of Delhi. They are credited with establishing the city of Delhi as their capital and laying the foundation of its urban and economic significance.
 
• The coin **“Dehliwal”** was used as currency during their rule and became an important symbol of economic activity in the region. *Hence, the correct answer is Tomaras.*
 
• The Tomaras ruled Delhi until they were overpowered by the **Chauhans**, another prominent dynasty in northern India during the medieval period.
 
• The **Dehliwal coins** were minted using silver, which was a widely accepted medium for trade during that era. These coins were instrumental in facilitating commerce in Delhi and surrounding areas.
 
• The legacy of the Tomaras, including their contribution to the development of Delhi as a political and economic hub, played a crucial role in shaping the city’s medieval history.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Tomara Dynasty:**

 
 
• The Tomara dynasty ruled Delhi from the **8th to the 12th century**. They were known for their military prowess and administrative skills, which helped them maintain control over the region.
 
• The Tomaras laid the foundation for Delhi’s importance by developing it as a center of **trade and commerce**. Their contributions were crucial in shaping the city's early medieval history.
 
 
 
• **Dehliwal Coins:**
 
 
• The Dehliwal coins were primarily made of **silver**, a valuable metal during medieval times. These coins were widely used for trade and were trusted due to their consistent weight and purity.
 
• The Tomaras initiated the minting of these coins to establish a stable monetary system in their territory, which facilitated economic growth.
 
• **Example:** These coins became a symbol of the flourishing trade network and economic stability of Delhi during the Tomara rule.
 
 
 
• **Other Dynasties Mentioned:**
 
 
• **Gahadavalas:** They ruled parts of Uttar Pradesh and Bihar during the medieval period but did not issue Dehliwal coins.
 
• **Khaljis:** The Khalji dynasty came later and was known for its military campaigns and administrative reforms, but they were not related to the issuance of Dehliwal coins.
 
• **Lodis:** The Lodis ruled Delhi during the late medieval period and were successors to the Khaljis. They were not associated with the Dehliwal coin either.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Historical Importance of Dehliwal Coins:**

 
 
• These coins symbolized the economic stability and strength of the Tomara dynasty’s rule in Delhi.
 
• The use of silver in minting these coins highlighted the region’s wealth and strong trade networks during the medieval period.
 
 
 
• **Legacy of Tomaras:**
 
 
• The Tomaras were instrumental in establishing Delhi as a prominent political and economic hub, a legacy that continued under subsequent dynasties.
 
• Their contributions laid the groundwork for Delhi’s importance in Indian history, which was later enhanced by the Chauhans, Khaljis, and Lodis.

questions.question: Which of the following Educational Event–Outcome pairs is correctly matched?

options.text: Charter Act of 1813 – Financial provision for education
Macaulay’s Minute (1835) – Promotion of Sanskrit studies
Orientalist–Anglicist Debate – Settled by Charter Act of 1833

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Charter Act of 1813 – Financial provision for education**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Charter Act of 1813:**

 
 
• The **Charter Act of 1813** was a landmark act in Indian education history as it provided the first-ever **financial provision for education** in India.
 
• It allocated a sum of **1 lakh rupees annually** for the promotion of education in British India, marking the beginning of state-sponsored education.
 
• This provision was aimed at promoting **Western education and science** in India.
 
• **Statement 1 is correct.**
 
 
 
• **Macaulay’s Minute (1835):**
 
 
• Thomas Babington Macaulay, in his famous **Minute on Indian Education** in 1835, advocated the promotion of **Western education** and suggested that the funds allocated should not be spent on promoting classical languages like **Sanskrit and Persian**.
 
• Macaulay’s emphasis was on imparting education in the **English language**, rather than promoting Sanskrit studies. Thus, the statement linking Macaulay's Minute with Sanskrit studies is **incorrect.**
 
 
 
• **Serampore Mission:**
 
 
• The **Serampore Mission**, led by missionaries such as **William Carey, Joshua Marshman, and William Ward**, was primarily involved in the promotion of vernacular education and the translation of religious texts.
 
• It was not associated with **elite military education**. Hence, this statement is **incorrect.**
 
 
 
• **Orientalist–Anglicist Debate:**
 
 
• The **Orientalist–Anglicist Debate** was a heated discussion on whether education in India should focus on traditional Indian knowledge (Orientalist view) or Western education and English language (Anglicist view).
 
• This debate was not settled by the **Charter Act of 1833**. Instead, it was largely addressed by Macaulay’s Minute in 1835. Thus, this statement is **incorrect.**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Charter Act of 1813:**

 
 
• This was the first time that the **British Parliament recognized the responsibility** of the East India Company to promote education in India.
 
• The Act marked a shift towards a more organized and state-sponsored approach to education in India.
 
 
 
• **Macaulay’s Minute (1835):**
 
 
• Macaulay was a strong proponent of **Western education** and believed in producing a class of Indians who would be "Indian in blood and color, but English in taste, in opinions, in morals, and in intellect."
 
• His views eventually led to the adoption of English as the medium of instruction in Indian educational institutions.
 
 
 
• **Serampore Mission:**
 
 
• The missionaries of Serampore were instrumental in translating the Bible into various Indian languages and promoting **vernacular education**.
 
• They established the **Serampore College** in 1818 to educate Indians in various disciplines, including theology.
 
 
 
• **Orientalist–Anglicist Debate:**
 
 
• The Orientalists, including figures like **William Jones** and **H.T. Colebrooke**, argued for the preservation and promotion of traditional Indian learning.
 
• The Anglicists, led by Macaulay, advocated for the adoption of Western education and English as the medium of instruction.
 
• The debate was resolved in favor of the Anglicists with the implementation of Macaulay’s recommendations in 1835.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Charter Act of 1813:** This was the first instance of **state intervention** in education in India, setting the stage for future educational policies.
 
• **Macaulay’s Minute:** It laid the foundation for the **Western education system** in India, which continues to influence the Indian education system to this day.
 
• **Serampore Mission:** It played a significant role in the **promotion of vernacular education** and the translation of texts into Indian languages.
 
• **Orientalist–Anglicist Debate:** This debate highlighted the differing perspectives on the nature and medium of education to be imparted in colonial India.

questions.question: Which option best reflects India’s diplomatic and operational stance on India–Myanmar boundary demarcation amid recent protests?

options.text: Arbitration through BIMSTEC under a 1987 treaty
Joint surveys and proposal of a Joint Boundary Working Group
Suspension of fencing to protect ASEAN trade
Complete dismissal of protests under AFSPA

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Joint surveys and proposal of a Joint Boundary Working Group**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• India’s approach to **boundary demarcation with Myanmar** is centered on **diplomatic collaboration**, ensuring stability and addressing concerns from both sides.
 
• **Joint surveys** are conducted to ensure accurate mapping of the boundary line, taking into account geographical, ethnic, and administrative considerations. This ensures the process is transparent and acceptable to both nations.
 
• The establishment of a **Joint Boundary Working Group** facilitates bilateral discussions and ensures that the demarcation process is mutually agreed upon without conflict. *Hence, statement 2 is correct.*
 
• India’s stance avoids unilateral actions like suspension of fencing or dismissing protests under laws like **AFSPA**. Instead, it focuses on dialogue and collaboration.
 
• The **Joint Boundary Working Group** also addresses concerns raised by local communities, ensuring their grievances are considered while demarcating boundaries.
 
• This approach reflects India's commitment to maintaining **peaceful relations** with Myanmar and ensuring that operational and diplomatic strategies align with regional stability.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• According to **Article 58** of the **Constitution of India**, a person must meet certain eligibility criteria to contest the **Presidential election** in India.
 
• One of the primary eligibility criteria is that the candidate must be at least **35 years of age**. This is a mandatory requirement to ensure maturity and suitability for the highest constitutional office in the country. *Hence, the correct answer is 35 years.*

questions.question:
Read the following statements about aerobic respiration:

Statement 1: Glycolysis takes place in the mitochondria.

Statement 2: The Krebs cycle occurs in the mitochondrial matrix.Statement

Statement 3: Oxygen acts as the final electron acceptor.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Only 2 and 3**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Statement 1: Glycolysis takes place in the mitochondria**

 
 
• **Glycolysis** is the first step of cellular respiration, where glucose is broken down into pyruvate, producing ATP and NADH.
 
• This process occurs in the **cytoplasm**, not in the mitochondria. Thus, this statement is **incorrect**.
 
 
 
• **Statement 2: The Krebs cycle occurs in the mitochondrial matrix**
 
 
• The **Krebs cycle** (or citric acid cycle) is the second stage of aerobic respiration, following glycolysis.
 
• This process occurs in the **mitochondrial matrix**, where acetyl-CoA is oxidized, producing ATP, NADH, and FADH2.
 
• Thus, this statement is **correct**.
 
 
 
• **Statement 3: Oxygen acts as the final electron acceptor**
 
 
• In the **electron transport chain** (ETC), electrons are passed through a series of protein complexes, creating a proton gradient across the inner mitochondrial membrane.
 
• **Oxygen** acts as the final electron acceptor in this process, combining with electrons and protons to form water.
 
• Thus, this statement is **correct**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Aerobic Respiration:**

 
 
• Aerobic respiration is a process of energy production that occurs in the presence of **oxygen**.
 
• It involves three main stages: **Glycolysis**, the **Krebs cycle**, and the **Electron Transport Chain (ETC)**.
 
• The main purpose of aerobic respiration is to generate **ATP**, which serves as the energy currency of the cell.
 
 
 
• **Steps of Aerobic Respiration:**
 
 
• **Glycolysis:** Occurs in the cytoplasm, where glucose is broken down into two molecules of pyruvate, yielding 2 ATP and 2 NADH.
 
• **Krebs Cycle:** Takes place in the mitochondrial matrix, producing ATP, NADH, and FADH2 as acetyl-CoA is oxidized.
 
• **Electron Transport Chain (ETC):** Occurs in the inner mitochondrial membrane, where NADH and FADH2 are used to generate a proton gradient that drives ATP synthesis. Oxygen serves as the final electron acceptor, forming water.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Oxygen:**
 
 
• **Oxygen** is essential for aerobic respiration as it ensures the continuation of the ETC by accepting electrons and preventing a backup of reduced carriers (NADH and FADH2).
 
• Without oxygen, cells switch to **anaerobic respiration**, which is less efficient and produces lactic acid or ethanol as byproducts.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Comparison of Aerobic and Anaerobic Respiration:**

 
 
• **Aerobic respiration:** Requires oxygen, produces up to 36-38 ATP per glucose molecule, and occurs in eukaryotic cells.
 
• **Anaerobic respiration:** Does not require oxygen, produces only 2 ATP per glucose molecule, and is common in prokaryotic cells and certain eukaryotes during oxygen deprivation.
 
 
 
• **Role of Mitochondria:**
 
 
• Mitochondria are known as the **powerhouses of the cell** as they generate most of the cell's ATP through aerobic respiration.
 
• Their structure includes a double membrane, with the **inner membrane** housing the ETC and the **matrix** facilitating the Krebs cycle.

questions.question: Which Article of the Constitution empowers Parliament to legislate on State List subjects in national interest?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 249**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 249** of the **Constitution of India** empowers **Parliament** to make laws on matters enumerated in the **State List**, provided it is deemed necessary in the **national interest**.
 
• This can be done when the **Rajya Sabha** passes a resolution by a majority of not less than two-thirds of the members present and voting, declaring that such legislation is essential in the national interest.
 
• Once such a resolution is passed, Parliament acquires the authority to legislate on that subject for a period of **one year**. This period can be extended by passing a similar resolution again. *Hence, Article 249 empowers Parliament to legislate on State List subjects in the national interest.*
 
• This provision is a mechanism to ensure that issues of national significance are addressed uniformly across the country, even if they fall within the State List.
 
• The resolution under **Article 249** does not remove the powers of the state legislature over the subject; it only gives concurrent powers to Parliament. *Hence, this article facilitates coordination between the Centre and the states.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Understanding Article 249:**

 
 
• **Article 249** provides flexibility to the federal structure of India by allowing the Parliament to intervene in state matters when the national interest is at stake.
 
• This article ensures that the **unity and integrity of the nation** are preserved, even in matters that are typically under state jurisdiction.
 
 
 
• **Examples of Article 249 being used:**
 
 
• This article has rarely been invoked, but it serves as a vital constitutional tool for addressing extraordinary situations.
 
• For instance, it might be used in cases of emergencies, such as handling issues related to national security, public health crises, or economic stability.
 
 
 
• **Comparison with other Articles:**
 
 
• **Article 253:** This article empowers Parliament to legislate for the implementation of international treaties, agreements, or decisions. It does not specifically deal with the State List.
 
• **Article 248:** This article gives Parliament exclusive powers to legislate on matters not enumerated in the Union List, State List, or Concurrent List (residuary powers).
 
• **Article 254:** This article addresses conflicts between laws made by Parliament and laws made by state legislatures in the Concurrent List, giving precedence to central laws.
 
 
 
• **Significance of Article 249:**
 
 
• It upholds the federal structure of India while allowing for a strong central authority in situations of national importance.
 
• The provision ensures that critical issues are addressed effectively, regardless of whether they fall under the State List.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Key Features of Article 249:**

 
 
• Requires a **two-thirds majority** in the Rajya Sabha to pass the resolution for legislating on State List subjects.
 
• The resolution remains valid for **one year** and can be extended further by passing another resolution.
 
 
 
• **Parliament's Powers in Context:**
 
 
• While Parliament gets concurrent power to legislate, the state legislatures retain their rights to make laws on the subject.
 
• Such legislation by Parliament is not permanent and is subject to the validity period of the resolution passed in the Rajya Sabha.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements:

Statement 1: The Production Possibility Frontier (PPF) illustrates opportunity cost and trade-offs.

Statement 2: PPF is used to calculate government revenue and expenditure.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Only Statement 1**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Statement 1:** The Production Possibility Frontier (PPF) illustrates opportunity cost and trade-offs.

 
 
• The **Production Possibility Frontier (PPF)** is an economic model that represents the maximum combination of two goods or services that an economy can produce, given available resources and technology.
 
• It highlights the concept of **opportunity cost**, which refers to the value of the next best alternative foregone when one option is chosen over another.
 
• The PPF also demonstrates the concept of **trade-offs**, as producing more of one good requires producing less of another due to limited resources.
 
• The curve typically has a concave shape, reflecting the law of increasing opportunity costs, as resources are not equally efficient in producing all goods.* Hence, Statement 1 is correct.*
 
 
 
• **Statement 2:** PPF is used to calculate government revenue and expenditure.
 
 
• This statement is **incorrect** as the **PPF** does not deal with government revenue or expenditure.
 
• The calculation of government revenue and expenditure falls under **fiscal policy** and involves concepts such as **taxation, public spending, and budget analysis**.
 
• The PPF is purely an economic model focusing on resource allocation and production capabilities, not government financial management.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Key Features of PPF:**

 
 
• The PPF curve is used to demonstrate **scarcity**, as it shows the limits of production based on available resources.
 
• It also illustrates **efficiency**; points on the curve represent efficient resource utilization, while points inside the curve indicate inefficiency.
 
• Points outside the curve are unattainable with the current level of resources and technology.
 
 
 
• **Real-Life Applications of PPF:**
 
 
• PPF is used to analyze trade-offs in resource allocation, for example, between consumer goods and capital goods in an economy.
 
• It helps businesses and policymakers understand the implications of decisions that involve reallocating resources, such as shifting focus from industrial to agricultural production.
 
 
 
• **Opportunity Cost in Detail:**
 
 
• Opportunity cost is a key concept in economics and is directly linked to the PPF. It refers to the cost of choosing one option over another in terms of the benefits that could have been gained from the foregone alternative.
 
• For instance, if an economy shifts resources from producing 100 units of wheat to producing 50 units of rice, the opportunity cost is the quantity of wheat forgone.
 
 
 
• **Important Points:**
 
 
• The PPF can shift outward if there is an improvement in resource availability or technology, indicating economic growth.
 
• A shift inward represents a decline in production capacity due to factors such as natural disasters or resource depletion.
 
• Fiscal policies, such as taxation and government spending, are unrelated to the PPF and are instead analyzed through budgetary and financial frameworks.

questions.question: Under the 2025 Index of Economic Freedom, which factor is assessed under the component “Government Size”?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Government spending levels**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Government Size** component in the **2025 Index of Economic Freedom** evaluates the degree of government intervention in the economy through expenditures, taxes, and enterprises.
 
• **Government spending levels** are a key metric under this component, which indicates the extent to which government consumption and expenditures affect economic growth. *Hence, this is the correct answer.*
 
• The aim of evaluating government spending is to determine how efficiently public resources are allocated and whether they promote a sustainable economic environment.
 
• The Index of Economic Freedom measures the size of government as one of its core components to assess the balance between public and private sector activities in the economy.
 
• Other factors like taxation and fiscal health also contribute to this evaluation, but government spending levels are a primary focus for gauging overall economic freedom under this category.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **About the Index of Economic Freedom:**

 
 
• The **Index of Economic Freedom**, published annually by the **Heritage Foundation**, evaluates the economic freedom of countries based on ten quantitative and qualitative factors grouped into four broad categories: **Rule of Law, Government Size, Regulatory Efficiency, and Market Openness**.
 
• This index helps policymakers, investors, and researchers understand the economic conditions of countries and their impact on growth and prosperity.
 
 
 
• **Government Spending in the Index:**
 
 
• The government spending indicator assesses public sector consumption as a percentage of GDP, aiming to measure its impact on the economy.
 
• Excessive government spending can lead to deficits, debt accumulation, and crowding out of private investment, which negatively impacts economic freedom.
 
• **Example:** Countries with high government spending relative to GDP, such as welfare states, often score lower on this metric due to reduced private sector activity.
 
 
 
• **Explanation of Other Options:**
 
 
• **Public education funding:** While education funding is a form of government expenditure, the Index does not specifically evaluate it under the "Government Size" component. Instead, it is categorized more broadly under government spending.
 
• **Defence expenditure:** Similar to public education, defence spending is an element of overall government expenditure, but it is not specifically analyzed as a standalone factor under this category.
 
• **Foreign aid allocation:** This is part of government expenditures, but like the previous options, it is not separately assessed under "Government Size."
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Government Spending Levels:**

 
 
• Countries with lower levels of government spending relative to GDP often have higher economic freedom scores, as excessive spending can lead to inefficiencies and distort market mechanisms.
 
• The component also evaluates whether public spending is directed towards productive investments or unproductive subsidies.
 
 
 
• **Examples:**
 
 
• **Singapore:** High economic freedom due to minimal government intervention and efficient public spending.
 
• **Sweden:** Despite high public spending, Sweden ranks well due to productive allocation and fiscal discipline.

• The **Second Five-Year Plan (1956-1961)** placed a major emphasis on the development of **heavy industries** in India. It was based on the **Mahalnobis Model**, which prioritized industrialization as a strategy to achieve economic growth.
 
• The main focus was on developing industries such as **steel, coal, cement, and heavy machinery**, which were considered essential for infrastructure development and economic self-reliance.
 
• This plan aimed to promote the establishment of **public sector enterprises** to drive industrial growth, as private capital was limited during that period.

• **First Five-Year Plan (1951-1956):**

• It prioritized investments in **dams, irrigation projects, and agricultural production**. For example, projects like **Bhakra Nangal Dam** were initiated.
 
 
 
• **Second Five-Year Plan (1956-1961):**
 
 
• This plan emphasized the growth of **heavy industries** and the expansion of the public sector to achieve self-reliance in industrial production.

• It also aimed to enhance the production of **coal, power, and machinery** to support industrialization.
 
 
 
• **Third Five-Year Plan (1961-1966):**
 
 
• The Third Plan focused on **self-reliance and poverty reduction**. It aimed to diversify the industrial base and increase agricultural production to meet the needs of the growing population.
 
• However, the plan's success was hampered by challenges like the **Indo-China War (1962)** and the **Indo-Pak War (1965)**, which diverted resources to defense.
 
 
 
• **Fourth Five-Year Plan (1969-1974):**
 
 
• The Fourth Plan focused on achieving **economic stability** and reducing income inequality.
 
• It aimed at improving agricultural productivity through the **Green Revolution** and investing in power and transport infrastructure.

questions.question: Economic liberalisation in India has its maximum impact on which sectors?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Secondary and Tertiary**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Economic liberalisation in India** refers to the process of opening up the economy to global markets by reducing government regulations, promoting privatization, and encouraging foreign investments. It began in **1991**.
 
• The liberalisation reforms had a significant impact on the **Secondary (Industrial) sector** and the **Tertiary (Service) sector** due to the focus on **industrial growth, technological advancements, and globalization.**
 
• The **Secondary sector** saw a boost as liberalisation encouraged **foreign direct investments (FDI)**, modernization of industries, deregulation of the manufacturing sector, and increased competition. *Hence, this sector was significantly impacted.*
 
• The **Tertiary sector**, which includes services such as **banking, IT, telecommunications, and trade**, experienced tremendous growth due to improved policies for foreign investment, privatization, and technological advancements in communication. *Hence, this sector was also highly impacted.*
 
• The **Primary sector** (agriculture and allied activities) was relatively less impacted by liberalisation policies as the focus was more on industrialization and service-oriented growth. *Hence, the impact on this sector was minimal.*
 
• ***Hence, the correct answer is Secondary and Tertiary.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Secondary Sector:**

 
 
• **Definition:** The Secondary sector includes manufacturing and industrial activities such as factories, construction, and production of goods.
 
• **Impact of Liberalisation:** Policies like removal of licensing requirements, encouragement of FDI, and export-oriented growth significantly boosted the Secondary sector.
 
• **Examples:** Growth in industries like **automobile manufacturing, pharmaceuticals, steel production**, and electronics was observed post-1991.
 
 
 
• **Tertiary Sector:**
 
 
• **Definition:** The Tertiary sector involves services such as banking, trade, telecommunications, IT, healthcare, and education.
 
• **Impact of Liberalisation:** Liberalisation brought globalization and technological advancements that transformed the service industry. The IT and software sectors, in particular, saw exponential growth.
 
• **Examples:** The emergence of Indian IT giants like **Infosys, TCS, Wipro**, and the expansion of telecom services (e.g., **BSNL, Airtel**) were directly linked to economic reforms.
 
 
 
• **Primary Sector:**
 
 
• **Definition:** The Primary sector includes agriculture, fishing, forestry, and mining activities.
 
• **Minimal Impact:** The focus of liberalisation was not on agriculture or allied activities, as these sectors continued to face challenges like low productivity and lack of modernization.
 
• **Examples:** Agricultural reforms like **Minimum Support Price (MSP)** were not directly related to liberalisation policies but were introduced to support farmers.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Liberalisation Policies:**

 
 
• **1991 Reforms:** India introduced policies like **industrial delicensing, reduction of tariffs, privatization** of public sector enterprises, and opening up the economy to foreign investments.
 
• **FDI Inflows:** Liberalisation led to a surge in **FDI inflows** in sectors like manufacturing, IT, and telecommunications.
 
 
 
• **Examples of Growth:**
 
 
• **IT Industry:** The Indian IT sector became a global leader, contributing significantly to GDP and employment.
 
• **Industrial Expansion:** Companies like **Tata Steel, Maruti Suzuki, and Reliance Industries** expanded their operations, leveraging liberalisation policies.

questions.question:
Read the below statements marked as Assertion (A) and Reason (R). Mark the correct option:

Assertion (A): India’s foreign exchange reserves increased sharply after the 1991 reforms.

Reason (R): Trade liberalisation led to higher exports and capital inflows.

options.text: Both A and R are true and R correctly explains A
Both A and R are true but R does not explain A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Both A and R are true and R correctly explains A**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Assertion (A): India’s foreign exchange reserves increased sharply after the 1991 reforms.**

 
 
• The 1991 economic reforms in India marked a turning point for the country's economic policies, leading to liberalization, privatization, and globalization.
 
• India faced a severe balance of payments crisis in 1991, and the reforms included measures to attract foreign investment and boost exports, which helped improve foreign exchange reserves significantly. *Hence, statement A is correct.*
 
 
 
• **Reason (R): Trade liberalization led to higher exports and capital inflows.**
 
 
• Trade liberalization was one of the key aspects of the 1991 reforms. By reducing import tariffs, eliminating import licensing, and promoting exports, India became more integrated into the global economy.
 
• Foreign capital inflows increased as the reforms made India an attractive destination for foreign direct investment (FDI) and portfolio investments. *Hence, statement R is correct.*
 
 
 
• Since trade liberalization and foreign capital inflows were key factors in boosting foreign exchange reserves, statement R correctly explains statement A. *Hence, the correct answer is "Both A and R are true and R correctly explains A."*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **1991 Economic Reforms:**

 
 
• The reforms were introduced under the leadership of then Prime Minister **P.V. Narasimha Rao** and Finance Minister **Dr. Manmohan Singh**.
 
• The balance of payments crisis forced India to pledge gold reserves and seek assistance from the **International Monetary Fund (IMF)**. The conditions of IMF loans mandated economic reforms.
 
• Key measures included **industrial deregulation, reduction in trade barriers, and opening up sectors to foreign investment**.
 
 
 
• **Foreign Exchange Reserves:**
 
 
• India’s foreign exchange reserves increased from a mere **$1.2 billion** in 1991 to over **$600 billion** by 2023.
 
• The reserves include foreign currency assets, gold reserves, Special Drawing Rights (SDRs), and the Reserve Tranche Position (RTP) with the IMF.
 
• Higher reserves provide economic stability and the ability to withstand external financial shocks.
 
 
 
• **Trade Liberalization:**
 
 
• Trade liberalization included reducing import duties, removing quantitative restrictions, and simplifying export procedures to enhance India's competitiveness.
 
• Exports grew significantly after the reforms, driven by sectors like **IT services, textiles, and pharmaceuticals**.
 
• Foreign capital inflows, including **FDI and Foreign Portfolio Investments (FPI)**, contributed to economic growth and reserve accumulation.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Balance of Payments Crisis:**

 
 
• India faced a severe balance of payments crisis in **1991**, with reserves dwindling to just **two weeks’ worth** of imports.
 
• The crisis was resolved through reforms and assistance from the **IMF**. Gold reserves were pledged to restore confidence in the economy.
 
 
 
• **Impact of Reforms:**
 
 
• **FDI inflows:** Increased foreign investment in sectors like telecom, infrastructure, and manufacturing.
 
• **Export growth:** Key export sectors, including **software services**, flourished due to competitive pricing and global demand.
 
• **Economic growth:** The reforms led to sustained economic growth rates of over **6%** annually during the 1990s.

 **Song-Theme (List – II)**

• The dance revolves around songs praising **Lord Jagannath** and other deities. *Hence, it is associated with theme B.*
 
 
 
• **Kalbelia Dance:**

• The dance is performed with songs that narrate stories of their lives, including themes of deserts and snakes. *Hence, it is associated with theme C.*
 
 
 
• **Tippani Dance:**

• The dance is accompanied by rhythmic songs, often showcasing themes of rural life and labor. *Hence, it is associated with theme D.*

questions.question:
Consider the following statements:

Statement 1: The Sixth Schedule applies to Nagaland and Arunachal Pradesh.

Statement 2: It grants legislative powers to autonomous district councils.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Only Statement 2**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Statement 1:** The **Sixth Schedule** of the Indian Constitution does not apply to **Nagaland** and **Arunachal Pradesh**. It applies only to the tribal areas in the northeastern states of **Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura, and Mizoram**. These provisions aim to protect the rights of tribal communities and provide them autonomy in governance. *Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.*
 
• **Statement 2:** The Sixth Schedule grants legislative powers to **Autonomous District Councils (ADCs)**. These councils are empowered to make laws on subjects like land, forests, water resources, agriculture, health, and more within their jurisdiction. ADCs act as mini legislatures for tribal areas and enable self-governance for these regions. *Hence, statement 2 is correct.*
 
• **Autonomous District Councils:** ADCs are established under the Sixth Schedule to the Constitution of India. They serve the purpose of creating self-governing institutions for the tribal population in the northeastern states. Examples include the Khasi Hills ADC in Meghalaya and the Chakma ADC in Mizoram.
 
• The Sixth Schedule provides special provisions for the administration of tribal areas to preserve their cultural and social practices and ensure their development without external interference.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Sixth Schedule:**

 
 
• The Sixth Schedule of the Indian Constitution was designed to govern tribal areas in northeastern states while preserving their unique cultural and social identities.
 
• It applies to **Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura, and Mizoram**, providing for the establishment of **Autonomous District Councils** (ADCs).
 
• ADCs have legislative, executive, and judicial powers within their jurisdiction and can create laws on various subjects such as land management, social customs, public health, and forest resource management.
 
 
 
• **Autonomous District Councils:**
 
 
• ADCs are empowered to administer tribal areas autonomously. They consist of elected and nominated members and have the authority to make regulations on various matters.
 
• Examples include the **Naga ADC** in Nagaland and the **Garo Hills ADC** in Meghalaya.
 
• ADCs aim to ensure self-governance and protect the rights of tribal communities, allowing them to manage their resources and traditions independently.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Significance of Sixth Schedule:**

 
 
• The Sixth Schedule empowers tribal communities to govern their areas independently, preserving their cultural and social practices.
 
• It helps in reducing external interference and ensures the development of tribal regions based on their unique needs.
 
• Tribal areas governed under the Sixth Schedule enjoy special autonomy and are often excluded from the applicability of other laws and regulations.
 
 
 
• **Difference from Fifth Schedule:**
 
 
• The Fifth Schedule applies to tribal areas outside the northeastern states and provides guidelines for the administration and control of these areas.
 
• Unlike the Sixth Schedule, the Fifth Schedule does not include provisions for autonomous councils but focuses on tribal welfare through state government intervention.

Consider the following statements about the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST):

Statement 1: It observes in near- and mid-infrared wavelengths.

Statement 2: It is positioned at the Sun–Earth L2 point.

Statement 3: It carries instruments for detecting exoplanets.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**All 1, 2 and 3**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Statement 1:** The **James Webb Space Telescope (JWST)** observes in **near-infrared** and **mid-infrared wavelengths**. This capability helps it peer through cosmic dust to study the formation of stars, galaxies, and planetary systems. *Hence, statement 1 is correct.*
 
• **Statement 2:** The JWST is positioned at the **Sun–Earth Lagrange Point 2 (L2)**, which is approximately **1.5 million kilometers** away from Earth. This location minimizes interference from the Earth, Moon, and Sun and provides a stable environment for observing deep space. *Hence, statement 2 is correct.*
 
• **Statement 3:** The JWST carries advanced instruments, including the **Near Infrared Spectrograph (NIRSpec)** and the **Mid-Infrared Instrument (MIRI)**, which are designed to detect and study **exoplanets**. These instruments allow scientists to analyze the atmospheres of exoplanets and search for potential signs of life. *Hence, statement 3 is correct.*
 
• ***Hence, the correct answer is All 1, 2 and 3.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **James Webb Space Telescope (JWST):**

 
 
• JWST is a **large infrared space telescope** launched by **NASA** on **December 25, 2021**, in collaboration with the **European Space Agency (ESA)** and the **Canadian Space Agency (CSA)**.
 
• Its mission is to study the **early universe**, galaxy formation, star formation, and exoplanetary systems.
 
 
 
• **Key Features:**
 
 
• JWST's **primary mirror** is made of **18 hexagonal segments** of **gold-plated beryllium**, with a total diameter of **6.5 meters**.
 
• Its instruments include **NIRCam**, **NIRSpec**, **MIRI**, and the **Fine Guidance Sensor**, which are optimized for detecting infrared light.
 
• Positioned at **L2**, it has an uninterrupted view of space, shielded from solar and terrestrial interference.
 
 
 
• **Applications:**
 
 
• JWST allows astronomers to study the **atmospheric composition** of exoplanets, including the presence of **water vapor, carbon dioxide, and methane**.
 
• It helps in understanding the **formation and evolution** of stars and galaxies.
 
• It provides insights into the **big bang era** and the **formation of the first galaxies**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Scientific Contributions:**

 
 
• JWST is designed to observe objects as far back as **13.5 billion years**, close to the time of the **big bang**.
 
• Its ability to detect **infrared wavelengths** makes it ideal for studying **star-forming regions** hidden behind cosmic dust.
 
 
 
• **Comparison with Hubble Space Telescope:**
 
 
• While the **Hubble** primarily observes in **visible** and **ultraviolet wavelengths**, JWST specializes in **infrared observations**.
 
• JWST has a larger mirror and is positioned farther from Earth, enhancing its ability to detect faint objects.
